entries.summary: Choose the files Auto Loader should ingest.
details: Use a storage path or glob. pathGlobFilter matches basenames; a SQL transform can handle filtering that the path pattern cannot express.
constraints: Provide this value for the selected action form. Validate the resolved flowgroup after applying templates, presets and substitutions.

entries.summary: Tell Auto Loader the format of the input files.
details: This key is mandatory even though the generator’s fallback is json. The value becomes cloudFiles.format.
constraints: Provide this value for the selected action form. Validate the resolved flowgroup after applying templates, presets and substitutions.

entries.summary: Auto Loader reads incrementally using streaming mode.
details: LHP supports stream for Auto Loader; batch is rejected. This is separate from whether the pipeline runs continuously.
entries.unsetBehavior: When the resolved action omits this field, the default is stream. A preset may supply a value before generation.

entries.summary: Choose a schema file to define the input columns.
details: A string here is a file path, not inline DDL. Choose source.schema, legacy schema_file or cloudFiles.schemaHints; do not combine them. Leave explicit schema sources unset to use inference.

entries.summary: Use the legacy schema-file setting for Auto Loader.
details: Prefer source.schema for new configurations. Do not combine this key with source.schema or cloudFiles.schemaHints.

entries.summary: Choose where Auto Loader stores its inferred schema state.
details: This is a schema tracking location, not the file that defines input columns. Do not also set the equivalent cloudFiles.schemaLocation option.

entries.summary: Infer specific data types while discovering input columns.
details: This maps to cloudFiles.inferColumnTypes. Do not also set that option under source.options.
entries.unsetBehavior: When the resolved action omits this field, the default is false. A preset may supply a value before generation.

entries.summary: Decide how Auto Loader handles newly discovered columns.
details: addNewColumns evolves the schema; rescue keeps new data in the rescued-data column; failOnNewColumns stops on a new column. Do not also set cloudFiles.schemaEvolutionMode.

entries.summary: Name the column used for rescued input data.
details: This legacy field maps to cloudFiles.rescueDataColumn in LHP. For the documented Auto Loader rescued-data option, prefer source.options.cloudFiles.rescuedDataColumn. Check the generated reader settings when migrating a legacy configuration.

entries.summary: Configure Auto Loader’s cloudFiles options.
details: Use cloudFiles.* option names. Inline DDL hints belong in cloudFiles.schemaHints, not source.schema. Legacy scalar options must not duplicate their cloudFiles equivalents.

examples.label: YAML example
examples.yaml:
source:
  options:
    cloudFiles.schemaHints: "order_id BIGINT, amount DECIMAL(18,2)"

entries.summary: Pass additional options directly to the Spark reader.
details: These keys are merged into the reader without a prefix. Keep Auto Loader cloudFiles settings and format-prefixed options in their appropriate sections.

entries.summary: Set options specific to the selected input format.
details: LHP prefixes each key with the selected format. For CSV, a delimiter entry becomes csv.delimiter.

entries.summary: Limit the number of files consumed in a micro-batch.
details: This maps to cloudFiles.maxFilesPerTrigger and helps control batch size. Do not also supply that key under source.options.

entries.summary: Name the intermediate view published by this action.
details: Downstream actions refer to this name through source or SQL. Use a distinct name that describes the data after this step.
constraints: Provide this value for the selected action form. Validate the resolved flowgroup after applying templates, presets and substitutions.

entries.summary: Choose the Unity Catalog catalog containing the source table.
details: Combine catalog, schema and table to identify the Delta table. Substitution tokens allow the catalog to vary by environment.

examples.label: YAML example
examples.yaml:
source:
  catalog: "${catalog}"
  schema: bronze
  table: orders

constraints: Provide this value for the selected action form. Validate the resolved flowgroup after applying templates, presets and substitutions.

entries.summary: Choose the Unity Catalog schema containing the source Delta table.
details: This is a schema name, not a schema-definition file. Pair it with source.catalog and source.table.
constraints: Provide this value for the selected action form. Validate the resolved flowgroup after applying templates, presets and substitutions.

entries.summary: Choose the table to read from the source database.
details: Provide a table name in the source system. The other connection settings determine which database is used.
constraints: Provide this value for the selected action form. Validate the resolved flowgroup after applying templates, presets and substitutions.

entries.summary: Choose a batch read or incremental streaming read.
details: batch uses a nonstreaming reader; stream uses a streaming reader. This does not set the pipeline’s continuous execution mode.
entries.unsetBehavior: When the resolved action omits this field, the default is batch. A preset may supply a value before generation.

entries.summary: Control how the Delta reader reads the table.
details: Use readChangeFeed: "true" only with streaming mode. Batch reads can use versionAsOf or timestampAsOf for time travel. Option values must be nonempty.

entries.summary: Filter the Delta source before publishing its view.
details: Provide filter clauses as a list. Keep column names consistent with the input table.

entries.summary: Select the source Delta columns needed downstream.
details: List the columns to retain. Leaving this unset preserves the source projection chosen by the reader.

entries.summary: Name the intermediate view published by this action.
details: Downstream actions refer to this name through source or SQL. Use a distinct name that describes the data after this step.
constraints: Provide this value for the selected action form. Validate the resolved flowgroup after applying templates, presets and substitutions.

entries.summary: Write the SQL query that loads data into this action’s target view.
details: Provide inline SQL or source.sql_path, not both. Environment substitutions work in either form.

entries.summary: Read the load query from an external SQL file.
details: Use this for a query maintained separately from the flowgroup. Remove source.sql when choosing the file form.

entries.summary: Name the intermediate view published by this action.
details: Downstream actions refer to this name through source or SQL. Use a distinct name that describes the data after this step.
constraints: Provide this value for the selected action form. Validate the resolved flowgroup after applying templates, presets and substitutions.

entries.summary: Choose the original Python module for this load action.
details: Use a .py file in the project. LHP copies the whole module and its supported local helper imports into generated output; edit the original file.
constraints: Provide this value for the selected action form. Validate the resolved flowgroup after applying templates, presets and substitutions.

entries.summary: Name the function that returns the loaded DataFrame.
details: The load function receives spark and a parameters dictionary. Additional helper functions can remain in the same module.

entries.summary: Pass named settings to the Python load function.
details: LHP passes the mapping as the function’s parameters dictionary. Use the value types expected by your function.

entries.summary: Name the intermediate view published by this action.
details: Downstream actions refer to this name through source or SQL. Use a distinct name that describes the data after this step.
constraints: Provide this value for the selected action form. Validate the resolved flowgroup after applying templates, presets and substitutions.

entries.summary: Locate the database using its JDBC connection URL.
details: Use the driver’s jdbc: URL format with host, port and database. Supply credentials separately as secret references.
constraints: Provide this value for the selected action form. Validate the resolved flowgroup after applying templates, presets and substitutions.

entries.summary: Select the JDBC driver class used for the connection.
details: Use the fully qualified class name matching the database and installed driver, such as org.postgresql.Driver.
constraints: Provide this value for the selected action form. Validate the resolved flowgroup after applying templates, presets and substitutions.

entries.summary: Supply the database user as a secret reference.
details: Use ${secret:scope/key}, for example ${secret:db/user}, to keep credentials out of committed YAML.
constraints: Provide this value for the selected action form. Validate the resolved flowgroup after applying templates, presets and substitutions.

entries.summary: Supply the database password as a secret reference.
details: Use ${secret:scope/key}, for example ${secret:db/password}. The scope/key identify the stored credential; do not place the password itself in project YAML.
constraints: Provide this value for the selected action form. Validate the resolved flowgroup after applying templates, presets and substitutions.

entries.summary: Read a table directly through JDBC.
details: Use a table identifier such as public.orders. Choose source.table or source.query, not both.

entries.summary: Use a JDBC query instead of reading a whole table.
details: Provide query or table, not both. The query runs against the database identified by the JDBC connection.

examples.label: YAML example
examples.yaml:
source:
  query: SELECT order_id, amount FROM public.orders

entries.summary: Name the intermediate view published by this action.
details: Downstream actions refer to this name through source or SQL. Use a distinct name that describes the data after this step.
constraints: Provide this value for the selected action form. Validate the resolved flowgroup after applying templates, presets and substitutions.

entries.summary: Choose the original Python module for this load action.
details: Use a .py file in the project. LHP copies the whole module and its supported local helper imports into generated output; edit the original file.
constraints: Provide this value for the selected action form. Validate the resolved flowgroup after applying templates, presets and substitutions.

entries.summary: Name the PySpark DataSource class in the chosen module.
details: The class implements the DataSource interface. Its name() result selects the reader format; streaming implementations provide a DataSourceStreamReader.
constraints: Provide this value for the selected action form. Validate the resolved flowgroup after applying templates, presets and substitutions.

entries.summary: Choose how Spark reads through your custom DataSource.
details: Set readMode on the action itself; source.readMode is not used for this load type. The default is stream.
entries.unsetBehavior: When the resolved action omits this field, the default is stream. A preset may supply a value before generation.

entries.summary: Pass options to the custom DataSource reader.
details: The keys and accepted values are defined by your DataSource implementation. LHP supplies the options mapping to the reader.

entries.summary: Name the intermediate view published by this action.
details: Downstream actions refer to this name through source or SQL. Use a distinct name that describes the data after this step.
constraints: Provide this value for the selected action form. Validate the resolved flowgroup after applying templates, presets and substitutions.

entries.summary: List Kafka brokers used to discover the cluster.
details: Use comma-separated host:port addresses. LHP maps this to kafka.bootstrap.servers; authentication options are supplied separately.
constraints: Provide this value for the selected action form. Validate the resolved flowgroup after applying templates, presets and substitutions.

entries.summary: Subscribe to one or more named Kafka topics.
details: Choose exactly one subscription method: subscribe, subscribePattern or assign. Kafka key/value payloads need deserialization in a downstream transform.

entries.summary: Subscribe to Kafka topics matching a regular expression.
details: Use this when topic names follow a pattern. Remove subscribe and assign when selecting pattern subscription.

entries.summary: Read explicitly selected Kafka topic partitions.
details: Provide the connector’s JSON topic-to-partition mapping as a string. Do not combine it with subscribe or subscribePattern.

entries.summary: Read new Kafka records as a stream.
details: LHP’s Kafka load requires stream; batch is rejected. Deserialize the binary key/value payload in a subsequent transform.
entries.unsetBehavior: When the resolved action omits this field, the default is stream. A preset may supply a value before generation.

entries.summary: Set additional Kafka connector options.
details: Use Kafka option names for authentication and reader behavior. Supply credentials through secret references rather than inline literals.

entries.summary: Name the intermediate view published by this action.
details: Downstream actions refer to this name through source or SQL. Use a distinct name that describes the data after this step.
constraints: Provide this value for the selected action form. Validate the resolved flowgroup after applying templates, presets and substitutions.

entries.summary: Choose the upstream view or views read by this transformation.
details: Use the target name of an earlier action. When multiple views are supported, keep their order consistent with the query or Python function.
constraints: Provide this value for the selected action form. Validate the resolved flowgroup after applying templates, presets and substitutions.

entries.summary: Write the SQL query used by this transformation.
details: Use the source view names in the query. For SQL transforms, stream(view_name) explicitly reads a streaming source. Choose inline SQL or sql_path.

examples.label: YAML example
examples.yaml: sql: SELECT * FROM v_orders WHERE amount > 0

entries.summary: Load the transformation query from a SQL file.
details: Choose a reusable .sql file and remove the inline sql key. Substitution tokens are supported in the file.

entries.summary: Name the intermediate view published by this action.
details: Downstream actions refer to this name through source or SQL. Use a distinct name that describes the data after this step.
constraints: Provide this value for the selected action form. Validate the resolved flowgroup after applying templates, presets and substitutions.

entries.summary: Choose the upstream view or views read by this transformation.
details: Use the target name of an earlier action. When multiple views are supported, keep their order consistent with the query or Python function.
constraints: Provide this value for the selected action form. Validate the resolved flowgroup after applying templates, presets and substitutions.

entries.summary: Choose the Python module implementing this transformation.
details: Use a project-relative .py path. Helper functions in the module are copied along with the selected entry function.
constraints: Provide this value for the selected action form. Validate the resolved flowgroup after applying templates, presets and substitutions.

entries.summary: Name the transformation’s Python entry function.
details: For one input, the function receives df, spark and parameters. With a source list, its first argument is the ordered list of DataFrames. Return a DataFrame.
constraints: Provide this value for the selected action form. Validate the resolved flowgroup after applying templates, presets and substitutions.

entries.summary: Pass named settings to the Python transformation.
details: The mapping is passed as one parameters dictionary, after the input DataFrame(s) and spark arguments.

entries.summary: Name the intermediate view published by this action.
details: Downstream actions refer to this name through source or SQL. Use a distinct name that describes the data after this step.
constraints: Provide this value for the selected action form. Validate the resolved flowgroup after applying templates, presets and substitutions.

entries.summary: Choose a batch read or incremental streaming read.
details: batch uses a nonstreaming reader; stream uses a streaming reader. This does not set the pipeline’s continuous execution mode.
entries.unsetBehavior: When the resolved action omits this field, the default is batch. A preset may supply a value before generation.

entries.summary: Choose the upstream view or views read by this transformation.
details: Use the target name of an earlier action. When multiple views are supported, keep their order consistent with the query or Python function.
constraints: Provide this value for the selected action form. Validate the resolved flowgroup after applying templates, presets and substitutions.

entries.summary: Choose the YAML file containing data-quality rules.
details: Each rule declares its predicate and action: warn, drop or fail. Quarantine mode coerces every rule to drop and routes rejected rows to the DLQ.
constraints: Provide this value for the selected action form. Validate the resolved flowgroup after applying templates, presets and substitutions.

entries.summary: Choose inline expectations or quarantine handling for invalid rows.
details: dqe applies the rules’ configured behavior. quarantine requires dlq_table and source_table and forces rules to drop.
entries.unsetBehavior: When the resolved action omits this field, the default is dqe. A preset may supply a value before generation.

entries.summary: Choose the table that stores quarantined rows.
details: Use a fully qualified DLQ table name. LHP derives the outbox name by appending _outbox. Recycling fixed rows requires Change Data Feed on the DLQ table.
constraints: Provide this value for the selected action form. Validate the resolved flowgroup after applying templates, presets and substitutions.

entries.summary: Identify the source table for quarantine tagging and recycling.
details: Use a fully qualified catalog.schema.table name. This is the business source table identity, not the temporary view consumed by the action.
constraints: Provide this value for the selected action form. Validate the resolved flowgroup after applying templates, presets and substitutions.

entries.summary: Name the intermediate view published by this action.
details: Downstream actions refer to this name through source or SQL. Use a distinct name that describes the data after this step.
constraints: Provide this value for the selected action form. Validate the resolved flowgroup after applying templates, presets and substitutions.

entries.summary: Choose the view to materialize as an intermediate table.
details: Use a source view name, or the supported mapping form. This temporary result is useful for later transformation steps.
constraints: Provide this value for the selected action form. Validate the resolved flowgroup after applying templates, presets and substitutions.

entries.summary: Optionally transform rows while materializing the temporary table.
details: The {source} placeholder expands to the chosen input. Without sql the action passes the source through. Use stream({source}) for streaming SQL.

entries.summary: Name the intermediate view published by this action.
details: Downstream actions refer to this name through source or SQL. Use a distinct name that describes the data after this step.
constraints: Provide this value for the selected action form. Validate the resolved flowgroup after applying templates, presets and substitutions.

entries.summary: Choose a batch read or incremental streaming read.
details: batch uses a nonstreaming reader; stream uses a streaming reader. This does not set the pipeline’s continuous execution mode.
entries.unsetBehavior: When the resolved action omits this field, the default is batch. A preset may supply a value before generation.

entries.summary: Choose the single view whose columns will be renamed or cast.
details: Use a plain view-name string. The old source.view mapping is not supported for schema transforms.
constraints: Provide this value for the selected action form. Validate the resolved flowgroup after applying templates, presets and substitutions.

entries.summary: Describe column renames, casts and selection inline.
details: Use the schema mapping syntax: old -> new: BIGINT renames and casts; col: TYPE casts; a bare column keeps it in strict mode. Choose this or schema_file.

examples.label: YAML example
examples.yaml:
schema_inline: |
  order_id: BIGINT
  total -> amount: DECIMAL(18,2)

entries.summary: Load the column transformation mapping from a schema file.
details: Use the schema-transform file format for renames and casts. Remove schema_inline when using a file.

entries.summary: Decide what happens to columns missing from the schema mapping.
details: strict retains only declared columns; permissive transforms declared columns and passes other columns through.
entries.unsetBehavior: When the resolved action omits this field, the default is permissive. A preset may supply a value before generation.

entries.summary: Name the intermediate view published by this action.
details: Downstream actions refer to this name through source or SQL. Use a distinct name that describes the data after this step.
constraints: Provide this value for the selected action form. Validate the resolved flowgroup after applying templates, presets and substitutions.

entries.summary: Choose a batch read or incremental streaming read.
details: batch uses a nonstreaming reader; stream uses a streaming reader. This does not set the pipeline’s continuous execution mode.
entries.unsetBehavior: When the resolved action omits this field, the default is stream. A preset may supply a value before generation.

entries.summary: Choose append, change-feed CDC or snapshot CDC writes.
details: standard appends rows; cdc applies ordered changes using keys and sequence information; snapshot_cdc compares full snapshots. Switching mode changes which configuration block is used.
entries.unsetBehavior: When the resolved action omits this field, the default is standard. A preset may supply a value before generation.

entries.summary: Choose the Unity Catalog catalog for the output table.
details: Combine catalog, schema and table to identify the destination. Environment substitutions can select different catalogs.

examples.label: YAML example
examples.yaml:
write_target:

  schema: silver
  table: orders

constraints: Provide this value for the selected action form. Validate the resolved flowgroup after applying templates, presets and substitutions.

entries.summary: Choose the Unity Catalog schema for the output table.
details: This is the destination schema name. Define column types separately with table_schema.
constraints: Provide this value for the selected action form. Validate the resolved flowgroup after applying templates, presets and substitutions.

entries.summary: Name the table created or updated by this write action.
details: The catalog and schema complete its destination. Use the same table identity when declaring downstream dependencies.
constraints: Provide this value for the selected action form. Validate the resolved flowgroup after applying templates, presets and substitutions.

entries.summary: Choose the input view or views feeding the table write.
details: Standard mode can append multiple source views. CDC consumes change rows. Snapshot CDC instead uses its own external snapshot source configuration.
constraints: Provide this value for the selected action form. Validate the resolved flowgroup after applying templates, presets and substitutions.

entries.summary: Identify the business key for matching changed rows.
details: Provide a nonempty list of natural-key columns. These keys identify records; they are different from partitioning or clustering columns.
constraints: Provide this value for the selected action form. Validate the resolved flowgroup after applying templates, presets and substitutions.

entries.summary: Order changes for each business key.
details: Choose the change-order column, or an ordered list of columns when supported. Use source sequence information so later changes can be applied correctly.

entries.summary: Choose whether CDC overwrites values or tracks history.
details: Type 1 keeps current values; Type 2 preserves history. Use the integer 1 or 2, not a quoted string.
entries.unsetBehavior: When the resolved action omits this field, the default is 1. A preset may supply a value before generation.

entries.summary: Keep existing values when a CDC update contains nulls.
details: Enable this when nulls in incoming updates mean no replacement value. Leave it off when nulls should overwrite existing values.
entries.unsetBehavior: When the resolved action omits this field, the default is false. A preset may supply a value before generation.

entries.summary: Identify CDC records that represent deletions.
details: Provide a SQL expression evaluated on change records, such as operation = 'DELETE'.

entries.summary: Identify change records that truncate the target table.
details: This predicate is not supported with SCD Type 2. Remove it before selecting Type 2.

entries.summary: Select the columns included in CDC updates.
details: Use either column_list or except_column_list. An explicit include list is useful when only a known set of source fields should reach the target.

entries.summary: Exclude source columns from CDC updates.
details: Use either except_column_list or column_list. Exclude change-control fields when they should not be part of the target dataset.

entries.summary: Choose the columns whose changes create history records.
details: Use either an explicit history include list or track_history_except_column_list, not both. This controls history tracking rather than output projection.

entries.summary: Exclude columns from triggering history records.
details: Use this instead of track_history_column_list when most business columns should be tracked. This is separate from except_column_list.

entries.summary: Identify the external table supplying full snapshots.
details: Snapshot CDC reads an external table or path, not a view defined by another action in the same pipeline. Choose source or source_function, not both.

entries.summary: Provide a function that returns versioned full snapshots.
details: Supply file and function, plus optional parameters. The function runs outside SDP’s decorated context and must read its source directly.

entries.summary: Choose the Python file implementing snapshot retrieval.
details: Use a project-relative path. The whole file is copied, preserving helper functions; it must read external data rather than an in-pipeline dataset.
constraints: Provide this value for the selected action form. Validate the resolved flowgroup after applying templates, presets and substitutions.

entries.summary: Name the function that returns the next snapshot and version.
details: A typical function receives latest_version and returns a DataFrame/version pair, or None to stop. Declared parameters are bound as keyword arguments.
constraints: Provide this value for the selected action form. Validate the resolved flowgroup after applying templates, presets and substitutions.

entries.summary: Bind named keyword arguments to the snapshot function.
details: Each entry is supplied through functools.partial, so the function must accept the corresponding keyword arguments. Environment substitutions resolve before binding.

entries.summary: Identify the business key for matching changed rows.
details: Provide a nonempty list of natural-key columns. These keys identify records; they are different from partitioning or clustering columns.
constraints: Provide this value for the selected action form. Validate the resolved flowgroup after applying templates, presets and substitutions.

entries.summary: Choose whether snapshot CDC keeps current values or history.
details: Use integer 1 for Type 1 or 2 for Type 2. This setting belongs to snapshot_cdc_config, separate from cdc_config.scd_type.
entries.unsetBehavior: When the resolved action omits this field, the default is 1. A preset may supply a value before generation.

entries.summary: Choose the columns whose changes create history records.
details: Use either an explicit history include list or track_history_except_column_list, not both. This controls history tracking rather than output projection.

entries.summary: Exclude columns from triggering history records.
details: Use this instead of track_history_column_list when most business columns should be tracked. This is separate from except_column_list.

entries.summary: Control whether this action declares the streaming table.
details: Keep this enabled for the action that creates the table. A separate append action can use an existing declaration. Snapshot CDC forces table creation.
entries.unsetBehavior: When the resolved action omits this field, the default is true. A preset may supply a value before generation.

entries.summary: Run this append flow once instead of as an ongoing stream.
details: Use this action-level flag for a one-time append flow. It does not set the job schedule or the pipeline’s continuous mode.
entries.unsetBehavior: When the resolved action omits this field, the default is false. A preset may supply a value before generation.

entries.summary: Keep the generated dataset temporary to the pipeline.
details: Temporary datasets are not tagged by the Unity Catalog tagging hook. Check whether the dataset needs to be published for other pipelines.
entries.unsetBehavior: When the resolved action omits this field, the default is false. A preset may supply a value before generation.

entries.summary: Describe the purpose and contents of the output dataset.
details: Write a useful table comment for consumers, such as the grain and business meaning. This is separate from the action’s internal name.

entries.summary: Choose columns for liquid clustering.

entries.summary: Let the platform choose liquid clustering columns.

entries.summary: Choose a storage path for the output table.

entries.summary: Set properties on the generated output table.

entries.summary: Apply Spark configuration to this generated dataset.

entries.summary: Build the materialized view from an existing source view.

entries.summary: Define the materialized view with an inline SQL query.

entries.summary: Configure the materialized view’s refresh policy.
